name: dev.telara/linear-cycle-health-monitor
description: Analyze one Linear team's recent cycles for delivery health: scope creep (issues added after a cycle started), carryover (issues still open past a cycle's end), stale in-progress issues, and completion rate, computed deterministically from cycle and issue timestamps. Designed to run on a recurring schedule; when given this primitive's own prior output for the same team, each cycle's metrics are diffed against that prior run so a trend can be seen without re-deriving it. Read-only; never creates, updates, or completes cycles or issues. No model reasoning is used anywhere in this workflow.

transform.program:
# recent_cycles.star -- bound the team's cycles to the most recent
# `lookback_cycles` by cycle number.
# Predeclared params: cycles (list of {id, number, name, starts_at, ends_at,
# completed_at}), lookback_cycles (int).
# Output via `result`: {cycles: [...]} sorted ascending by number.

def _sorted_by_number(cycles):
    # Manual sort (not the builtin `sorted`) to avoid depending on this
    # runtime's exact keyword-argument support for a sandboxed Starlark
    # dialect; cycle counts per team are small so an O(n^2) pass is fine.
    items = list(cycles)
    n = len(items)
    for i in range(n):
        for j in range(0, n - i - 1):
            if items[j].get("number", 0) > items[j + 1].get("number", 0):
                items[j], items[j + 1] = items[j + 1], items[j]
    return items

def _recent(cycles, lookback_cycles):
    ordered = _sorted_by_number(cycles)
    n = len(ordered)
    start = n - lookback_cycles
    if start < 0:
        start = 0
    return ordered[start:n]

result = {"cycles": _recent(cycles, lookback_cycles)}

# cycle_health.star -- bucket team-scoped issues into cycles and compute the
# four deterministic health metrics per cycle. Pure arithmetic; no reasoning.
#
# Predeclared params:
#   cycles              list of {id, number, name, starts_at, ends_at, completed_at},
#                        already bounded + sorted ascending by number (recent_cycles.star)
#   issues              list of {id, status_type, created_at, updated_at, ...} for the
#                        whole team (list_issues, relay-paginated, all pages)
#   as_of               ISO 8601 timestamp string, this run's reference "now"
#   stale_after_days    int
#   risk_threshold_pct  int
#
# Output via `result`: {cycles: [...]}, each a fully-populated cycle record minus
# delta_vs_previous (added later by verdict.star).
#
# CATALOG-GAP APPROXIMATION (see README SPEC-FEEDBACK #2, #8): Linear's catalog
# exposes no per-cycle issue listing and no cycle_id field on an issue record, so
# true issue-to-cycle membership cannot be fetched. This bucketing is a heuristic:
# an issue is assigned to the LAST (most recent, since cycles arrive sorted
# ascending) cycle whose date window it overlaps -- created at/before the cycle's
# end, and last touched at/after the cycle's start -- giving each issue at most one
# assigned cycle. It is not a guaranteed-correct partition of Linear's own cycle
# assignment, only a best-effort proxy from timestamps the catalog does expose.

def _jdn(date_str):
    # Fliegel & Van Flandern proleptic-Gregorian Julian Day Number, computed with
    # only +,-,*,// -- this sandbox exposes no datetime/time module to do this for
    # us (see README SPEC-FEEDBACK #7). date_str's first 10 chars are "YYYY-MM-DD".
    y = int(date_str[0:4])
    m = int(date_str[5:7])
    d = int(date_str[8:10])
    a = (14 - m) // 12
    y2 = y + 4800 - a
    m2 = m + 12 * a - 3
    return d + (153 * m2 + 2) // 5 + 365 * y2 + y2 // 4 - y2 // 100 + y2 // 400 - 32045

def _days_between(later, earlier):
    return _jdn(later) - _jdn(earlier)

def _assign_cycle(issue, cycles):
    assigned = None
    created = issue.get("created_at")
    updated = issue.get("updated_at")
    for c in cycles:
        if created <= c.get("ends_at") and updated >= c.get("starts_at"):
            assigned = c.get("id")
    return assigned

def _metrics_for_cycle(cycle, bucket, as_of, stale_after_days):
    n = len(bucket)
    ended = cycle.get("completed_at") != None or cycle.get("ends_at") <= as_of

    scope_creep_n = 0
    completed_n = 0
    carryover_n = 0
    stale_n = 0
    for i in bucket:
        if i.get("created_at") > cycle.get("starts_at"):
            scope_creep_n += 1
        st = i.get("status_type")
        if st == "completed":
            completed_n += 1
        if ended and st != "completed" and st != "cancelled":
            carryover_n += 1
        if st == "started":
            days = _days_between(as_of, i.get("updated_at"))
            if days >= stale_after_days:
                stale_n += 1

    scope_creep_pct = 0
    completed_pct = 0
    carryover_pct = None
    if n > 0:
        scope_creep_pct = (100 * scope_creep_n) // n
        completed_pct = (100 * completed_n) // n
        if ended:
            carryover_pct = (100 * carryover_n) // n

    return {
        "issue_count": n,
        "scope_creep_pct": scope_creep_pct,
        "carryover_pct": carryover_pct,
        "stale_issue_count": stale_n,
        "completed_pct": completed_pct,
        "is_ended": ended,
    }

def _risk_flags(metrics, risk_threshold_pct):
    flags = []
    if metrics["scope_creep_pct"] > risk_threshold_pct:
        flags.append("scope_creep")
    if metrics["carryover_pct"] != None and metrics["carryover_pct"] > risk_threshold_pct:
        flags.append("carryover")
    return flags

def _build(cycles, issues, as_of, stale_after_days, risk_threshold_pct):
    buckets = {}
    for c in cycles:
        buckets[c.get("id")] = []
    for i in issues:
        cid = _assign_cycle(i, cycles)
        if cid != None and cid in buckets:
            buckets[cid].append(i)

    out = []
    for c in cycles:
        bucket = buckets[c.get("id")]
        m = _metrics_for_cycle(c, bucket, as_of, stale_after_days)
        flags = _risk_flags(m, risk_threshold_pct)
        out.append({
            "id": c.get("id"),
            "number": c.get("number"),
            "name": c.get("name"),
            "starts_at": c.get("starts_at"),
            "ends_at": c.get("ends_at"),
            "completed_at": c.get("completed_at"),
            "is_current": not m["is_ended"],
            "is_ended": m["is_ended"],
            "issue_count": m["issue_count"],
            "metrics": {
                "scope_creep_pct": m["scope_creep_pct"],
                "carryover_pct": m["carryover_pct"],
                "stale_issue_count": m["stale_issue_count"],
                "completed_pct": m["completed_pct"],
            },
            "at_risk": len(flags) > 0,
            "risk_flags": flags,
        })
    return out

result = {"cycles": _build(cycles, issues, as_of, stale_after_days, risk_threshold_pct)}

inputs.name: as_of
inputs.description: Reference timestamp this run treats as "now" for staleness and cycle-status calculations

inputs.name: lookback_cycles
inputs.description: How many of the team's most recent cycles (by cycle number) to analyze

inputs.name: page_size
inputs.description: Page size for the underlying issue-listing call

inputs.name: previous_run_output
inputs.description: This primitive's own output from its previous scheduled run for the same team; omitted or null on the first run

inputs.name: risk_threshold_pct
inputs.description: scope_creep_pct or carryover_pct strictly above this value flags a cycle at_risk

inputs.name: stale_after_days
inputs.description: Days of no update on an in-progress issue (relative to as_of) before it counts as stale

inputs.name: team_id
inputs.description: Linear team UUID to monitor this run
